title: PM2: `instances: 2` without `exec_mode` runs in cluster mode, and `pm2 jlist` lists each worker separately
summary: Setting instances to more than one makes PM2 choose cluster_mode even when exec_mode is not set. Tools that read `pm2 jlist` see one entry per worker with the same name, so they count or display the app twice.
body_markdown:
## What happens (reproduced)
An ecosystem entry with `instances: 2` and no `exec_mode`:
```
$ pm2 jlist | jq -r '.[] | select(.name=="app") | .pm2_env.exec_mode'
cluster_mode
cluster_mode
```

## Consequences
- Do not "fix" such an app to fork mode because its file never mentions cluster: it is already running as a cluster.
- Scripts over `pm2 jlist` should group by `name`. Status: any worker not `online` means the app is not online. Memory and restarts: sum them.
